title: fix(plugins): avoid Gateway stalls during source preparation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway event-loop stalls when plugin preparation creates source/native capture directories and their physical staging tokens on a filesystem waiting for a transaction commit.

Related: #200136, #200193, #200216. The motivating Team incident (25c97908, 2026-11-16 05:02 PST) blocked the Gateway MAIN thread for 1.97 seconds in `openat2(O_CREAT)` under `scheduler:update.remote-model-catalog`; the kernel waited in `btrfs_create → start_transaction → wait_current_trans`. The catalog's redundant lock was removed separately. This change handles the remaining physical capture-root owner.

## User Impact

Plugin preparation can wait on filesystem creation while the Gateway event loop remains responsive. There is no configuration or schema change and no operator action required.

The tradeoff is explicit: measured cold owner time increases from 183.267 to 453.257 ms, warm owner time from 141.459 to 182.479 ms, and whole process-tree CPU from 1,050 to 1,310 ms. A separate loaded-addon profile on the preceding revision observed 127.828 MiB RSS in the retained broker (summed process RSS increased 120.922 MiB; shared pages and profiling overhead included). The final revision proves ordinary same-process restarts reuse that broker; it does not remeasure that RSS observation. These costs are accepted for removing filesystem-transaction stalls from the Gateway thread, not described as an overall speedup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing broker resource owner now creates and retains the physical source/native roots and staging tokens. Preparation workers borrow paths; host cache and recovery leases retain the physical custody after execution ends. Loaded native code keeps its token until host exit. Ordinary Gateway restarts reuse the existing broker, and a fresh source replaces permanently failed or sealed authority without reopening old claims or inventing cleanup receipts.

This is the smallest complete root-custody cutover: moving only mkdir would leave token creation and lifetime operations on MAIN. Production grows by 685 lines across 21 production modules plus a net-zero build import adjustment. Twenty of those lines complete the shared lease type and preserve source-acquisition error classification across the new broker boundary. The growth is the private resource adapter and lifetime handoff; the old parent allocation callback and duplicate independent-resource count are removed. Existing pool/dependency declarations are moved intact to keep their owning modules within the repository's limits. No new manager, cache, database table or public protocol is introduced.

This does not claim all Gateway filesystem work is asynchronous. Recovery-copy/binding, runtime-selected synchronous JS/CJS/native imports, and the existing native-load realpath observation remain separate work.

## Evidence

The real preparation boundary records 28 synchronous root operations on the exact parent, including seven mutations, and zero on the candidate. Actual two-second source/native `mkdtempSync` faults move from the Gateway process into the broker: fault-interval heartbeat gaps are 2,029/2,010 ms before and 7/7 ms after; whole-operation candidate maxima are 14/12 ms. Existing physical custody and cleanup assertions remain active.

The timing and injected-delay results below were measured on runtime source corresponding to `03b70d95e1d71ab021158898cbcc06eaea7568a1`. Subsequent CI repairs preserve the create algorithm while correcting error projection, the shared lease type, and a broker sender binding, and removing an unnecessary await of a synchronous commit. These are prior-revision performance measurements, supported by focused regression proof of the changed paths, rather than a claim that final-head bytes were remeasured.

Canonical built Node 26.12.1/APFS proof used a synthetic surrounding 35 GiB agent database, 5,000 sessions and 62,000 workspace files; this owner does not scan those unrelated files. No Team data was copied. Five A1/A2 controls and five A/B pairs each include cold and warm phases (20 processes); four additional processes exercise the actual source/native faults. All 24 processes, observed brokers and source/artifact verification joined successfully. No samples were discarded. Host one-minute load was 9.376–11.450; tails are retained rather than attributed to noise.

| Metric, median (p95) | Parent | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold owner ms | 183.267 (188.857) | 453.257 (520.810) |
| Warm owner ms | 141.459 (145.714) | 182.479 (199.514) |
| Warm preparation ms | 135.386 (139.533) | 136.144 (147.538) |
| Warm retirement ms | 6.073 (6.310) | 47.427 (57.649) |
| Cold MAIN CPU ms | 30.188 (31.737) | 26.220 (30.325) |
| Warm MAIN CPU ms | 14.153 (15.320) | 7.827 (9.243) |
| Cold MAIN allocation MB | 30.943 (31.248) | 14.589 (16.491) |
| Warm MAIN allocation MB | 22.608 (25.778) | 6.557 (8.737) |
| Whole process-tree CPU ms | 1,050 (1,340) | 1,310 (1,440) |

Main allocation excludes the broker, so it is not a global memory-saving claim. A/A cold owner medians were 186.086/184.935 ms, warm 147.092/145.145 ms, and tree CPU 1,060/1,050 ms.

Rerunnable workload: build each pinned checkout with `pnpm build sourcePerformance`, then run `node --expose-gc scripts/perf/plugin-capture-custody-measure.mjs --repo <built-checkout> --fixture <synthetic-fixture> --label <arm>`. Use `--fault source` or `--fault native` with `--delay-ms 2000` and candidate `--expect-off-main` for the injected faults. The driver and preload are included in this PR.

<details>
<summary>Synthetic fixture setup and repeatable workload</summary>

Create the surrounding fixture once with the existing generator, outside the measured window:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/catalog-publication-measure.mjs \
  --state-dir /absolute/new-fixture --create --sessions 5000 --database-gib 35 \
  --workspace-files 62000 --workspace-file-bytes 17742 --samples 1
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --input-type=module - /absolute/new-fixture/physical <<'NODE'
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
const root = path.resolve(process.argv[2]);
fs.mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true });
process.env.OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR = path.join(root, 'fixture-setup-state');
process.env.OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH = path.join(root, 'absent-config.json');
const { createFixture, nativeSize } = await import('./src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.admission.test-support.ts');
const { bytes, ...fixture } = createFixture(path.join(root, 'source'), false);
if (bytes.length !== nativeSize) throw new Error('Unexpected synthetic native payload size');
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, 'fixture.json'), JSON.stringify({ fixture, nativeSize }) + '\n');
NODE
```

Build baseline and candidate separately. Invoke the candidate's committed driver against each built `--repo`, with unique labels and the same `--fixture /absolute/new-fixture/physical`. Run A1/A2/A/B five times serially, then A/B for each source/native fault. Wrap each process in `/usr/bin/time -l` for the whole-tree CPU column. Preserve source/build hashes and every JSON row. The synthetic payload is 2 MiB; real addon loading and post-exit reclaim are separately proven by the focused lifecycle test.

</details>

Focused proof covers the original main-thread guard, preparation cancellation/deadline/settlement, physical cache retention, real addon loading and reclaim exclusion, old-lease/successor overlap, ordinary same-process restart reuse, and actual broker-loss recovery. The sealed-only intermediate candidate failed the real process-loss regression; the final owner predicate passes all 17 lifecycle and 18 transport-retirement cases. A test-only watcher barrier timed out during validation; it now uses a bounded async sentinel wait under the unchanged deadline, and all four affected/cascading cases passed. Final affected types, lint, formatting and independent Codex reviews pass.

Before the CI-repair commit, full `pnpm check:changed --staged --base 2435c1faa791de766688ba27ca7a14a92e30b7e4` passed every gate except dead exports: 113 identities match the exact parent, plus one task-owned benchmark export. The benchmark now uses an explicit shared installer; its targeted script-export scan, lint/format and all four baseline/candidate source/native fault qualifications pass. The 113 parent findings remain a failed local gate, not a green result or an automatic CI waiver. Exact-head CI and final-head zero-open ClawSweeper review are required before landing.

The first exact-head CI run, 43987530227, found incomplete consumer migrations: a missing wrapper inventory entry, stale capture-root observations and low-space injection, an overbroad physical commit return type, an unregistered fixed protocol export, a new lint suppression, and test-line growth. The repair restores the existing contracts. The real broker low-space test also exposed lost source-acquisition classification before session creation; forwarding that existing fact restores startup containment while leaving transport and cleanup failures fatal. No failures from that CI run are claimed inherited. Repair head `d82c6f178d6b4cb1c09de4974664cd5140fb3f88` passes focused regressions, production types and all affected test type graphs, type-aware lint, formatting, the export-owner guard, the 400-line test budget without allowance, and independent Codex review. Its CI run completed with only the static type-cycle failure described below; ClawSweeper cleared all six items on that head.

Local provisioning covers 16 of the 17 Linux CI failures; the remaining filesystem case is platform-specific and remains CI proof. The selector also included a Darwin-only full cold/warm sibling case already known to have an unexplained timeout: it exceeded its 120-second deadline, reporting 202.398 seconds while synchronous subprocess work finished. That local failure is retained and is not classified inherited; its passing sibling cases are not a claimed fix. No full provisioning replay or blind CI rerun was performed.

CI run 43995776480 on `d82c6f1` passed the previously failing checks but exposed one static type dependency cycle between admission state and the lease module. Head `274e2ab300d4866700dec1891bf67dbe2e60568f` moves the unchanged contract into an import-free type leaf and updates all four consumers. The exact Madge guard now reports zero cycles; core types, type-aware lint, format and independent Codex review pass. This five-file change contains no executable behavior change and does not require remeasuring the prior performance results. Final-head CI and ClawSweeper re-review remain required; no inherited-failure exception is claimed.
